customer_name: Superior Court of California of the County of Orange
business_problem: Separate case-management systems, Excel-heavy reporting, and difficult statewide aggregation limited the court's ability to manage staffing, backlog, and cross-county reporting securely.
solution_summary: The Superior Court of California, County of Orange, built a centralized analytics foundation on Snowflake Data Cloud on Azure to unify case-management data across civil, criminal, traffic, family, juvenile, and probate systems. Instead of managing on-premises, hybrid, and cloud-only silos separately, the court standardizes definitions and lands data in one secure repository that serves as the local source of truth. Power BI and Tableau dashboards on top of Snowflake give administrators, judges, and staff detailed visibility into filings, hearings, jury activity, and caseflow. Snowflake Secure Data Sharing then extends governed subsets to the Judicial Council of California so 58 counties can aggregate data statewide without brittle file-transfer processes or loss of local control. The architecture supports workload forecasting, staffing, funding advocacy, and backlog analysis while preserving privacy, lineage, and operational trust.

solution_components.name: Snowflake Data Cloud
solution_components.role: Centralizes case-management data from multiple court systems into one governed analytics platform on Azure.

solution_components.name: Snowflake Secure Data Sharing
solution_components.role: Shares approved statewide datasets with California judicial bodies without manual file transfers.

solution_components.name: Power BI
solution_components.role: Provides operational dashboards for staffing, filings, hearings, and backlog analysis.

solution_components.name: Tableau
solution_components.role: Supports additional self-service analytics and drill-down reporting on court operations.

data_flow: Case-management data from multiple court systems is standardized and loaded into Snowflake on Azure. Power BI and Tableau expose local caseflow metrics, while Secure Data Sharing sends approved statewide datasets to judicial stakeholders for cross-county aggregation and funding analysis.
business_outcome: Orange County improved workload planning and service delivery, reduced backlog, became the template for statewide court data sharing, and helped secure $60 million in California funding for backlog reduction.
architecture_clues: Standardized data definitions unify separate case systems.
Snowflake runs on Azure as the court's centralized analytics environment.
Statewide sharing is governed through Secure Data Sharing rather than SFTP-like exchanges.
